evidence.V1: Half-timbered panel on a stone plinth reads instantly in front and three-quarter; silhouette and top are a clean wall slab with the cap overhang, which is the expected read for a straight wall piece.
evidence.V2: Big plaster wall, medium post/rail/brace timber frame and cap beam, small plinth blocks: clear three-tier hierarchy.
evidence.V3: Confident stylised half-timber: chunky timbers, chevron braces, overhanging cap beam and heavy plinth; only the brace butt ends are cut square rather than fitted into the post/sill joints.
evidence.V4: Timbers, cap beam and plinth blocks all carry consistent small chamfers that pick up highlight lines in the face and top close-ups.
evidence.V5: Face, end-section and top close-ups are clean: no z-fighting between timber and plaster, no pinches or stray faceting.
evidence.V6: Timber brown in two values, cream plaster and one grey stone for the plinth; disciplined and readable in slate and brick colourways.
evidence.V7: 408 tris vs module target 800 (ceiling 2000): well under target.
evidence.V8: Single white vertex-colour material, chamfered made edges, timber secondary + cream plaster + stone per the modular kit; T1 tiling pass.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Box, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner origin.

top_fixes: Fit the brace ends into the post/sill corners (angled cuts) instead of square butt ends that clip the joint
Wrap a corner post or timber edge onto the end faces so exposed wall ends are not a flat plaster slab
Optionally add a small accent (gold peg/iron strap) so the piece has a kit accent like other modular pieces
